result.summary: The intersection is equipped with high-visibility continental crosswalk markings and overhead traffic signals within a residential context. However, the environment lacks dedicated pedestrian signal heads and features potential sightline obstructions from vehicles parked close to the crossing.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Vehicles
hazards.description: A silver SUV is parked near the intersection corner, potentially blocking the line of sight between drivers and pedestrians waiting to cross.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the intersection, near the crosswalk entrance.

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Signal Heads
hazards.description: No dedicated pedestrian signals are visible at this signalized intersection, forcing pedestrians to rely on vehicular signals which may not provide adequate clearance intervals.

interventions.title: Intersection Daylighting
interventions.description: Restrict parking within 20-30 feet of the crosswalk to improve visibility between pedestrians and motorists.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Install dedicated pedestrian signal heads with countdown timers to clearly communicate the remaining crossing time.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane to shorten the crossing distance and place pedestrians in a more visible position before they enter the roadway.

result.summary: The image shows a wide multi-lane intersection with marked continental crosswalks and overhead traffic signals. While basic pedestrian infrastructure like sidewalks and curb ramps are present, the long crossing distance across the arterial road and the lack of a median refuge create significant exposure for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Long Crossing Distance
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross at least four lanes of traffic without a refuge island, increasing exposure time to vehicles.
hazards.location_in_image: Across the main roadway in the center of the intersection.

hazards.name: High-Speed Roadway Geometry
hazards.description: Wide, straight travel lanes on the arterial road encourage higher vehicle speeds through the intersection.
hazards.location_in_image: Main roadway (Bustleton Ave) stretching into the distance.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Install a raised median or refuge island to allow pedestrians to cross one direction of traffic at a time and provide a safe waiting area.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Construct bulb-outs at the corners to shorten the crossing distance and slow down right-turning vehicles.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval (LPI)
interventions.description: Program the traffic signals to give pedestrians a 3-7 second head start before the parallel vehicle traffic gets a green light.

result.summary: The intersection is equipped with basic pedestrian infrastructure including marked zebra crosswalks, sidewalks, and traffic signals within a residential context. However, the wide roadway width and lack of median refuge islands increase the exposure time and risk for pedestrians crossing the main thoroughfare.

hazards.name: Long crossing distance
hazards.description: The width of the main roadway requires pedestrians to be exposed to traffic for a significant duration without a mid-block refuge.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground crosswalk across the main road.

hazards.name: Wide curb radii
hazards.description: The corners appear designed for higher-speed vehicle turns, which can reduce driver yielding and increase the risk of collisions with pedestrians.
